description: Atomic facts from validation round 3 (2026-11-26): basil first cut vs regrowth cut, and tilapia FCR evidence. Candidates until Ajit approves them. Reliability recorded per AGENTS.md 6A.

facts.statement: In UVI staggered raft production, basil yielded 1.2 kg/m2 (167.1 g per plant) at the first harvest 28 days after transplant and 2.4 kg/m2 (327.1 g per plant) at the regrowth harvest; the authors note slow growth after transplanting while plants became established.

context.system: UVI commercial-scale coupled DWC raft, staggered weekly planting, 8 plants/m2, cut at 15 cm

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: UVI research report (published as Acta Horticulturae 648).
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Measured at the anchor site and density, but the same paper's batch system shows no first-cut penalty, and two raft trials elsewhere show none either.

facts.statement: In UVI batch raft production, basil yields per harvest were 2.1, 2.0, 1.7 and 2.0 kg/m2 (first harvest after transplant, then three regrowth harvests; production period about 28.3 days), so the first harvest was not lower than later ones.

context.system: UVI coupled DWC raft, batch planting of the whole 214 m2, 8 plants/m2

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Direct table values; conflicts with the same paper's staggered result (VR3_0001), so the context (batch vs staggered planting) matters and the cause is not stated.

facts.statement: In an aquaponic floating raft at 20 plants/m2, two-week-old basil seedlings gave 32.4 g fresh weight per plant at the first cut (35 days after planting) and 44.4 g at the second cut (79 days); the cut had no significant effect on fresh yield.

context.system: coupled aquaponic floating raft, cold greenhouse under 75 percent shade net

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Direct table values, n = 3; per day the first cut is close to the second (0.92 vs 1.01 g/d, our arithmetic), but light fell between the cuts.

facts.statement: In a hydroponic basil trial at 23 plants/m2, fresh yield was higher at the first cut (47 days after transplant) than at the second (75 days); the abstract gives a yield reduction of about 20 percent.

context.system: hydroponic, pots on benches in a glasshouse, mean air 26 C

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Per-cut values are only in a figure; the -20 percent is the abstract's figure. Direction agrees with VR3_0002 and VR3_0003.

facts.statement: In a backyard tilapia unit with gravel ebb-and-flow beds in a northern German glasshouse in autumn, basil grown from three-week-old rockwool seedlings averaged 16.1 +/- 13.8 g fresh biomass after 70 days at pH 8.0; the authors attribute below-expectation plant growth mainly to the high alkaline pH.

context.species: basil (Kiepenkerl seed, cultivar not named), mixed with mint and parsley at 18 plants/m2

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Large spread (SD 86 percent of the mean); the pH attribution is the authors' view, not a controlled test.

facts.statement: At UVI, tilapia fed ad libitum three times daily on a 32 percent protein diet over six harvests had feed conversion ratios of 1.71 to 1.92 (mean 1.79), with water about 24 C in winter and spring and 29 C in summer.

context.species: Nile and red tilapia, fingerlings about 70 g, 24-week cycles

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Measured over six harvests; matches SRAC 454's 'usual' 1.7 and the SRAC 282 and FAO 589 range of 1.4 to 1.8.

facts.statement: Khater et al. 2023 report tilapia FCR of 0.92 to 1.20 (40 g fingerlings, 60 days, 23.4 to 23.6 C) but do not print feed intake, and their FCR equation divides feed intake by per-fish gain times the final fish count, so the values cannot be recomputed.

context.system: coupled troughs with foam rafts, hydraulic loading 1.2 to 3.0 m/day

source_metadata.section_id: Methods Eq. 5 and fish results table

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Peer-reviewed, but the fish results table was read through a fetch summary and feed intake is missing.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Below the Tier 1 range (1.4 to 1.8) and UVI's 1.71 to 1.92 with no stated reason.

facts.statement: Studies disagree on how tilapia FCR changes below the growth optimum: Azaza et al. 2008 found FCR best at 26 and 30 C (vs 22 and 34 C), Mirea 2013 found FCR rising with temperature from 20 to 30 C, and Workagegn 2014 found feed use worst at 24 C (of 24 to 34 C).

source_metadata.section_id: review text; Workagegn via The Fish Site

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Read through a peer-reviewed review and a Tier 3 trade summary; primary tables not read.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: No numbers read from the primary papers; the directions conflict.
